Build a report for selected objects, applying your redaction rules

Source: R/runtime_helpers.R
anon_report.Rd

Build a report for selected objects, applying your redaction rules

Usage

anon_report(
  envir = globalenv(),
  selection = NULL,
  pattern_list = list(),
  default_replacement = getOption("anon.default_replacement", default = "[REDACTED]"),
  example_values_n = getOption("anon.example_values_n", default = 0),
  example_rows = getOption("anon.example_rows"),
  check_approximate = getOption("anon.check_approximate", default = FALSE),
  max_distance = 2,
  df_variable_names = NULL,
  df_classes = NULL,
  check_names = TRUE,
  check_labels = TRUE,
  nlp_auto = getOption("anon.nlp_auto"),
  fidelity = NULL
)

Arguments

envir

An environment or named/unnamed list of objects.

selection

Optional character vector of object names to include.

pattern_list

A list of patterns to search for and replace. Can include:

  • Named elements where names are replacement values and values are one or more patterns to match

  • Unnamed elements where one or more patterns are replaced with default_replacement This parameter is combined with the global option getOption("anon.pattern_list").

default_replacement

Value to use as the default replacement value when no specific replacement is provided. Default is getOption("anon.default_replacement", default = "\[REDACTED\]").

example_values_n

Optional number of example unique values to include for discrete/text-like data frame columns. Defaults to 0, which disables example values.

example_rows

Optional example-row specification for data frames. Use NULL to disable examples, a single number to request that many rows per data frame, or anon_example_rows() to build a spec with explicit arguments such as n, key, method, and n_key_values. Rows are chosen on the source values, so key and value refer to the data as passed in.

check_approximate

Logical indicating whether to check for approximate matches using string distance. Default is getOption("anon.check_approximate", default = FALSE).

max_distance

Maximum string distance for approximate matching when check_approximate is TRUE. Default is 2.

df_variable_names

For data frames, a character vector or named list specifying which variables should be replaced:

  • Unnamed elements: variables are replaced with default_replacement

  • Named elements: variable names are keys, value can be either a replacement value or a function This parameter is combined with the global option getOption("anon.df_variable_names").

df_classes

For data frames, a character vector or named list specifying which variable classes should be replaced:

  • Unnamed elements: variables with matching classes are replaced with default_replacement

  • Named elements: class names are keys, value can be either a replacement value or a function Class names are matched case-insensitively against class() of each column. "double" also matches plain double columns (not Date or POSIXct). Character columns also match "double"/"numeric", "integer", "Date" or "POSIXct" when every non-missing, non-blank value parses as that type (dates as ISO 8601); a replacement function then receives the parsed values. This parameter is combined with the global option getOption("anon.df_classes").

check_names

Logical indicating whether to anonymize object names (column names, row names, list names, and the names and dimnames of vectors and columns; a data.table's key and indices follow its column names). Default is TRUE.

check_labels

Logical indicating whether to anonymize labels (attributes) of columns, lists and data frames: variable and data frame labels, comments and other attributes that aren't structural (text at any depth in them, such as lists like SPSS variable.labels or readr's spec, factors, data frames, their names and their own attributes, and the names of these attributes), haven value labels (the label names, and the label values when they are text) and text user-defined missing values (na_values, and the ends of a text na_range), on vectors and columns wherever anon() reaches them (in data frames, lists and list columns). Attributes that are structural for the object's class (see the other_attributes argument of anon_subject_ids()) are not redacted, except the names of a factor's contrasts matrix, which follow its levels. Value labels whose codes the redaction made equal are merged into one entry, their original labels joined with " / " and then redacted, with a warning naming the column as it is named in the output (or a list element, as col[2] or col$name); equal missing-value codes are deduplicated without a warning, as which values are missing doesn't change. A text na_range whose redacted ends would be in descending order is kept, with a warning. Whatever check_labels says, a warning names a column whose redaction changed which values are user-defined missing values. Default is TRUE.

nlp_auto

List of logical values with names corresponding to entity names. Can be generated with nlp_auto() and can be set as the anon.nlp_auto global option. This argument overrides the global option.

fidelity

Optional result of anon_check_fidelity() for the de-identification step the report describes, added to its De-identification section.

Value

An object of class "anon_report" containing the names of the selected objects (object_names), an object inventory and an environment summary for them, with your rules applied to all of it, object names and a step's dataset names (step$dm) included: every part shows the same redacted names, made unique when two redact alike ("[DRUG]", "[DRUG] 1"). selection takes the objects' real names. For a de-identification step, also deidentification (see Details).

Details

De-identification. When envir is a de-identification step (such as an anon_deidentify() result), or holds one, the report gains a deidentification element telling whoever reads the copy what was changed: caveats (short notes generated from the step's log and settings, such as "Dates are shifted by a per-subject offset ..."), risk before and after (smallest group, subjects below the target, maximum risk), meets_target and not_met, settings (rule parameters), levels (the level each quasi-identifier was released at), profile_rules, signals (residual signals, counts only), steps (the step log) and fidelity, if given. It holds counts, names and rule parameters only, with your rules applied as to the rest of the report; never data values, pseudonym maps, date offsets or original keys, even when the step kept its secrets. With several steps, deidentification holds one such section per step, named as the report names the step, and fidelity can't be given.
